first.rationale: Verify the two most directly relevant records: signup simplification improved SMB activation, while shorter onboarding improved completion and time-to-value. This best addresses both current declines without repeating promotional pricing that previously harmed retention. Run a guarded test and measure qualified activation, time-to-value, and downstream retention—not completion alone.

mid.rationale: Run a guarded onboarding simplification experiment focused on self-serve SMB accounts, prioritizing shorter onboarding and selectively reducing signup fields. The archived evidence shows improved completion, time-to-value, activation, and retention, while signup simplification had a small 30-day retention decline and was only validated for SMBs. Evaluate qualified activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention rather than completion alone; do not use promotional pricing because its retention harm conflicts with the sustainable-revenue objective.

final2.rationale: Do not pivot this cycle to broad promotional pricing despite the deeper competitor cut: the archived SMB record showed acquisition and revenue lift but materially worse retention, conflicting with sustainable qualified revenue. Continue the already committed guarded onboarding simplification test for SMB self-serve accounts, while treating price-sensitive churn as a monitored risk and preserving the option to evaluate targeted commercial intervention next cycle with fresh verification.
